tieu_de: Saturn transit through the 6th house: hard work that pays later
mo: Why is my work so heavy right now?
How can I avoid burning out?

If you feel like you are doing more than ever at work and nobody seems to notice, check where Saturn is in your chart. Its passage through the 6th house is famous for heavy workloads, long lists and effort that goes unrewarded in the short term.
The good news is that the effort is not wasted. What you build now becomes the working foundation you rely on for years. The trick is to keep going without burning yourself out.

doan: The 6th house governs daily work, routines, duties, the systems you use to get through the week, and the habits that keep your body going. Saturn brings responsibility and structure here, which usually means more tasks and higher standards.

Recognition is often slow. You may take on extra duties, cover for colleagues or build processes that others use, without praise or pay rising to match. Saturn is laying groundwork, and groundwork is rarely visible. Keeping your commitment steady matters more than being thanked.
Daily habits also come under review. Stress from work can spill into sleep, eating and energy, so looking after yourself becomes part of the job.
Planet Saturn Rules Capricorn Discipline, responsibility, structure
Your inbox grows. Meetings multiply. You become the person who knows how things work, and so everything comes to you. Some people take on a role with more responsibility but the same title.
You may start noticing how your routines affect you: the late nights, skipped meals, the coffee that replaces lunch. Tiredness that used to pass quickly may linger.

Many people find comfort in small, steady things during this transit. Caring for a pet, volunteering, or doing something useful for others can bring a sense of meaning that the day job does not always provide.

This is a strong period to master your craft. Skills practised daily under Saturn become second nature. Systems you build now, whether a filing method, a workflow or a morning routine, can carry you for a decade.
It is also a good time to reset your habits around rest, food and movement. Changes made slowly and kept up for months tend to stick.
People who work steadily through this transit often find that the recognition arrives later, sometimes when Saturn reaches the top of the chart.
Overwork is the obvious risk. It is easy to say yes to everything and end up drained. Frustration at not being recognised can also sour your attitude to work you would otherwise enjoy.
Another trap is perfectionism. Saturn raises standards, and if you apply those standards to every small task, you may never feel finished.

Saturn stays in a sign for about 2.5 years, and its time in a house is roughly similar. Because house sizes vary by house system and latitude, your own 6th house transit may be shorter or longer. Retrograde periods can bring it back over the same ground, so work pressures may come in waves.
Keep a record of what you do. Lists of completed projects, problems solved and hours covered become evidence when it is time to ask for recognition later.
Set limits on availability. Decide when work stops each day and hold that line as often as you can. Delegate where possible, even if others do things differently.

Look after the basics. Sleep, regular meals, moderate exercise and real breaks are not luxuries during this transit. If stress is building, act early by talking to someone or reducing your load before it becomes a crisis. For anything physical that worries you, see a qualified professional.
Stop measuring yourself by immediate feedback. Watch for resentment and deal with it directly, through a conversation or a change in duties, rather than letting it harden.
Saturn in the 6th house brings more duty to daily work. It often coincides with added responsibilities, higher standards or covering gaps that others leave.
Usually, but not right away. Saturn tends to reward consistent work later rather than sooner. Keeping records of what you achieve makes that recognition easier to claim.
Set clear limits on work hours, protect rest, and build simple daily habits that support your energy. Asking for help or reducing your load early is far easier than recovering from exhaustion later.
